transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep snapping at people. Like at work, during a safety meeting, I just started yelling before I could stop myself. Now the younger inspectors seem scared to ask me anything, and… I don’t want to keep being like that.
When did you first notice yourself snapping at people like this?
It started after that machinery accident, when they changed us to the overnight schedule. So… about two years and four months ago. That’s when I first noticed I was snapping at people like this.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to act on?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get upset and I react, but I don’t have any specific thoughts or urges that I feel like I have to act on over and over.
Do you find yourself repeating certain behaviors over and over?
No, I don’t think I do. I haven’t noticed myself repeating certain behaviors over and over like that.
Do you have trouble managing your emotions?

Yes. That’s honestly why I’m here. I keep snapping at people. Like at a safety meeting, I started yelling before I could stop myself, and now the younger inspectors act scared to even ask me anything.
Do you ever feel like you have to do something very specific to reduce anxiety or stress?
No, not really. I mean, I get stressed, but I don’t have some specific thing I feel like I have to do to make it go away.
Do you consider yourself a perfectionist?
I don’t know that I’d call myself a perfectionist. I like things done right, especially at work, but I don’t think I’m obsessive about everything being perfect.
Do you have any habits or rituals that you feel are hard to change?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve got routines like anybody does, but nothing I feel stuck doing or that I can’t change if I have to.
Do you feel like you're in control when you snap at people?

No. Not when it happens. It’s like I’m already yelling before I’ve decided to. That’s part of why I’m here—I keep snapping at people. At a safety meeting, I started yelling before I could stop myself, and now the younger inspectors seem scared to ask me anything.
Do you feel like you're able to think before you react when you snap at people?

Not really. By the time I realize what I’m doing, I’m already snapping. Like that safety meeting—I was yelling before I could stop myself, and now the younger inspectors act like they’re afraid to even ask me things.
Do you often feel overwhelmed by your emotions?

Yes. I get overwhelmed, especially when I’m angry. It comes on fast, and I snap before I can get a handle on it. That safety meeting is a good example—I started yelling before I could stop myself, and now the younger inspectors seem scared to ask me anything.
Do you feel like snapping at people has become a habitual way for you to deal with stress or frustration?

Yeah… I think it has. When I get stressed or frustrated, I go straight to snapping before I even think. That’s why I’m here. Like at that safety meeting, I started yelling before I could stop myself, and now the younger inspectors act scared to ask me anything.
Do you feel like you're trying to achieve something specific when you snap at people, or is it more of an automatic reaction?

It’s more automatic. I’m not trying to get something out of it, really. I just get worked up and I’m already snapping before I can stop myself. That’s what happened in that safety meeting—I started yelling, and now the younger inspectors seem scared to even ask me anything.
Do you feel like snapping at people helps you feel more in control of a situation?

Maybe for a second, yeah. When I snap, it feels like I’m taking control because I’m loud and people stop. But honestly, it’s not really control. I’m here because I keep doing that—like at the safety meeting, I started yelling before I could stop myself, and now the younger inspectors seem scared to ask me anything.
Do you think your snapping at people is part of a broader way you interact with others in general?

Yeah, I think it is. It’s not just one bad moment. I keep snapping at people when I get worked up. Like I said, at that safety meeting I started yelling before I could stop myself, and now the younger inspectors act scared to ask me anything. That bothers me, because I don’t want to be that kind of person.
Do you think you've always had a tendency to snap at people, even before the machinery accident?

No, not like this. I mean, I could get annoyed before, sure, but I wasn’t snapping at people all the time. Now I get worked up and it just comes out before I can stop it. That safety meeting was a good example—I started yelling, and now the younger inspectors seem scared to even ask me things.
Do you think your way of snapping at people is something that's become a part of who you are, rather than just a reaction to specific situations?

I don’t know if I’d say it’s who I am, but it’s starting to feel like something I do too often now. I’m here because I keep snapping at people. That safety meeting still bothers me—I started yelling before I could stop myself, and now the younger inspectors seem scared to ask me anything.
Do you think you would still snap at people if you changed jobs or were in a different social environment?

I think it might still happen, yeah. It doesn’t feel like it’s just the job itself. I’m here because I keep snapping at people, and that safety meeting kind of showed it—I started yelling before I could stop myself. Now the younger inspectors act scared to ask me anything, and that really bothers me.
Do you think your tendency to snap at people is something that has been a part of your personality for most of your life?

No, I don’t think it’s been part of me my whole life. I’m here because I keep snapping at people now, like at that safety meeting where I started yelling before I could stop myself. And now the younger inspectors act scared to ask me anything, which… that’s not how I want to be.
Do you think you would still consider yourself someone who snaps at people even when you're not stressed or frustrated?

Not really when I’m calm, no. It’s more like I get frustrated and then I snap before I can stop myself. That’s why I’m here — like at that safety meeting, I started yelling, and now the younger inspectors seem scared to come ask me anything.
